# CLI

<!-- generated by `mop dev docs` from the commandlets' docstrings: edit the docstring, not this file -->

Every command of `mop`, as its commandlet in `mop/cli` describes itself: the first line of the docstring is what `mop help` lists, the whole docstring is the command's usage.

## Client

Run on a client: an operator's machine or a master shell.

### core: commands

#### mop add

```text
create a puppet: mop add [git-origin] --role <role>

Without origin, the origin of the current working copy is used. The name is
picked automatically: <project>-<number>; placement over the pool and the
8 GB reservation are not chosen here. Silent when the puppet is running; on
a terminal it shows the current step. The new puppet is in mop list.
Use mop models to see model IDs offered by the selected proxy.

--role names the new puppet's role (soul name): the creation carries a
request_id, the answer is checked against the server's echo of the role
triple. A role principal (a grant master) names the role and sends no
bootstrap policy of its own: the child inherits the parent's approved
snapshot. A roleless add is gone: every puppet carries a soul.

--request-id retries an earlier unknown outcome under its id: the server
reconciles to the job it reserved instead of creating a second one; a
changed payload under the same id is refused before any effect.
```

#### mop attach

```text
open a terminal on a puppet: mop attach <name>

Reconnects to a running puppet and creates nothing: a new one is
`mop add` or `mop <role>`. Detaching (or a dropped connection) leaves the
puppet running. Goes over ssh, not the bus: a live terminal is not
something a bus verb hands over.
```

#### mop code

```text
launch claude outside the pool: mop code [claude options]

Same session environment as `mop master`, none of the pool. No project, no
bus credentials, no mop MCP server: this is an ordinary claude session on
the installation's LLM proxy. Use it where the pool has nothing to do with
the job — a scratch checkout, someone else's repository, a shell on a
machine that never got `mop server deploy`.

Everything goes to claude as-is
(`mop code --continue` resumes the last session here). The command won't
mirror claude's own flags: there are dozens of them, and the list would drift
the moment claude ships a new version.

Permissions are skipped, same as `mop master` and the puppets: the session
comes up with --dangerously-skip-permissions added for you. The whole point
of the command is to get to work on a provider without ceremony, and
answering a prompt per shell call is exactly the ceremony. Passing the flag
yourself is harmless — it isn't added twice.

The session uses the selected server's LLM proxy. Its URL and key come from
the server profile, connection.json saved by mop login; missing credentials
start login before claude. With multiple joined servers, name one with
--server. Without a terminal, missing input refuses. This command never adds
the pool's MCP tools.
```

#### mop delete

```text
delete a puppet: mop delete <name> [--force]

Where the body is the node itself, the clone stays and is reused if a puppet
of that name comes back; where it is a container, the body goes with the
puppet — memory and disk with it.

Another master's puppet (work in its clone, or dispatched minutes ago) is
refused with that master's name; --force acts anyway and says whose it was.
```

#### mop diagnose

```text
mop diagnose: offline summary of the selected server login

Prints which server the next command would talk to, where that choice
came from (command line, environment, clone binding, or the sole joined
directory), where its login directory is, and whether the login is whole:
complete, empty (no whole connection.json; leftovers of the old
operator.json+client.json pair are no login) or a machine service
identity. No network, no prompts, no writes; the login's secrets are
never shown. The schema line names the version of a validated
connection.json only; other formats carry no schema claim.

Broken or conflicting directories refuse with exit code 1 -- the refusal
is the diagnosis. empty/machine are informational: exit code 0 with an
explicit not-ready line, not a success message.
```

#### mop landing

```text
landing token of this project: mop landing [take <puppet>|give|show] [--force]

  mop landing                   who holds the token, if anyone
  mop landing take pu-mop-3     grant the token to pu-mop-3 before it lands
  mop landing give              take it back on the puppet's report
  mop landing take pu-mop-3 --force
                                take it from a gone master; says whose it was
  mop landing give --force      release a gone master's token

Exactly one puppet between merge and push per project: two parallel pushes
race, and the second bounces non-fast-forward. take refuses while another
master holds the token, naming who and since when; asking again for the same
puppet is not an error. The holder is your login on the bus; a holder that
went away is released with --force.
```

#### mop list

```text
pool puppets: who's where, busy or free, what LLM it runs on

"free" means the clone has no unsaved work, not that the session is silent:
the dispatch decision rests on this.
```

#### mop master

```text
launch the master role as a new pooled puppet: mop master [git-origin]

The same launcher as `mop <role>` for the role master, and the command
says so: a new puppet of the project is registered with the role, waits
for its bootstrap and the role's session, and the terminal attaches to it
over ssh. Detaching leaves the puppet running; reconnect with
`mop attach <name>`, which never creates one. Only origin belongs to a
role launch: the role owns its prompt, settings and permissions, and any
flag is refused before anything is allocated. A failure after
registration names the created puppet and does not create another.

Any other role of the catalogue launches the same way: `mop <role>`. A
role whose name is a mop command or a reserved bus name is refused before
anything is allocated. The local claude launch is gone: a master is a
pooled puppet; for claude outside the pool there is `mop code`.
```

#### mop models

```text
list models offered by the selected LLM proxy: mop models

Reads the live /v1/models catalog using the selected server's client key.
The key is never printed. The proxy catalog may include models that Claude
Code cannot use; this command does not test model compatibility.
```

#### mop profile

```text
mop profile: show the pool role, project and integration branch

The role comes from bus credentials, not the presence of MCP tools. An unset
integration branch is reported as unset; it is not inferred from origin/HEAD.
A role principal is profiled by its bundle's role name — a grant is a puppet,
not a master of anything.
```

#### mop recycle

```text
recreate a puppet on a clean working copy: mop recycle <name> [--force]

Unsaved changes are wiped by restoring from git, the target directory is
removed entirely (the first build after a recycle is slow). The clone
itself isn't recloned. The puppet's workspace (.mop/bootstrap.yaml) comes
from the working copy this runs in, or from the origin elsewhere. A role
principal recycles without one: the server keeps the approved policy.

Another master's puppet (work in its clone, or dispatched minutes ago) is
refused with that master's name; --force acts anyway and says whose it was.
```

#### mop restart

```text
restart a stuck puppet: mop restart <name> [--force]

The clone and branch survive a restart — the wrapper comes up on the same
directory.

Another master's puppet (work in its clone, or dispatched minutes ago) is
refused with that master's name; --force acts anyway and says whose it was.
```

#### mop send

```text
send a message to a pool puppet or a session on this machine

  mop send <target> <text>            send
  mop send <target> -                 text from stdin
  mop send <target> <text> --wait[=N] send and wait until the recipient goes free
  mop send --list                     live sessions on this machine

<target> — puppet name (pu-<project>-1), session name, pid, directory, or socket
path. A puppet is recognized by the pu- prefix and reached over the bus; anything
else is a local session, reached directly through its uds inbox.

  --priority now|next|later   where in the recipient's queue (default next)
  --mode bypass|prompting     which permission mode to present as (bypass)
  --quiet                     silent, exit code only
  --force                     take over a puppet another master leads

Channel protocol — CHANNEL.md, bus subjects — BUS.md.
```

#### mop stat

```text
token usage across the pool, a bar per day: mop stat [--days N] [--puppets|--users]

Sums claude token counters (input, output, cache write, cache read) over
every puppet on every ready node for the last N days (default 14), by the
node's local date. --puppets breaks the same window down per puppet, the
biggest spender first, instead of drawing the chart; --users does it per
person -- the login of the master whose message started each turn, "-" for
spend nobody's message started, or a node whose agent does not attribute yet. Read off the puppets'
own transcripts, so a puppet whose clone was removed no longer counts. In a
master shell the picture is the project's, not the pool's.
```

#### mop stop

```text
stop a puppet job: mop stop <name>

Operator only. Stops initialization, the current session and automatic
restarts. The container, clone and bootstrap workspace are kept.
Use mop update <name> to start the job again. This is not Escape for
interrupting a Claude turn, and it does not delete the puppet.
```

#### mop tail

```text
tail of a puppet's screen: mop tail <name> [-n N] [-f] [--startup]

-n N       how many lines (default 10)
-f         keep following until Ctrl-C
--startup  operator-only initialization log before the session; wrapper stages
           and bootstrap tasks, not project command output
```

#### mop update

```text
update a puppet: mop update <name> [git-origin] [--fresh] [--force]

Changes what's named and keeps the rest: without origin the puppet stays on
its repository. By default the claude that comes up resumes the directory's
last conversation; --fresh brings it up with a clean session. An allocation
restart doesn't reread the spec, and treatment is a restart — a treated
puppet isn't obliged to come back into the context it got stuck on.

Another master's puppet (work in its clone, or dispatched minutes ago) is
refused with that master's name; --force acts anyway and says whose it was.

A role principal updates without a client policy: the live puppet
keeps its own approved snapshot, and the wire carries no workspace text.
```

#### mop wipe

```text
wipe a puppet's working copy: mop wipe <name> [--force]

The clone is reset to HEAD (unsaved and untracked changes are gone), the
target directory is removed entirely. The agent refuses if the tmux session
is alive: a bare wipe is for a stopped puppet — the full cycle is mop recycle.

Another master's puppet (work in its clone, or dispatched minutes ago) is
refused with that master's name; --force acts anyway and says whose it was.
```

### pool: administration

#### mop login

```text
log in to a pool server: mop login [login] [--server host] [--https-port port]

Server and login come from --server/LOGIN, the process environment or the
working copy's binding; if missing, they are asked for. The bus password is
asked without echo (or read from MOP_BUS_PASSWORD) and verified before
saving. A valid previous login is reused.

The HTTPS port uses --https-port, the saved client port, MOP_HTTPS_PORT or
443, in that order, without prompting; a sole joined server is selected when
none is named. Join also fetches the server's LLM proxy URL and client key
and verifies them before saving; rejoining refreshes a rotated key without
replacing working credentials.

The server's certificate is pinned before the bus password is sent; compare
the fingerprint on the controller: openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256
-in ~/.config/mop/secrets/tls.pem

Credentials stay in separate private files under
~/.config/mop/servers/<server>/. The clone remembers only server and login
in local git config. --user NAME is the old spelling of LOGIN.
```

#### mop setup

```text
this operator machine's own dependencies: mop setup

Sets up the machine you work with the pool from, and nothing for the pool:
ansible (to run this very setup), git, pip and the python libraries mop is
written on, and a word about claude if it is not in PATH. The server has
its own: mop server setup.

Ansible does the work, as everywhere else in mop: this command only
installs ansible itself through apt when it is missing (Debian 13 ships
the full ansible package, collections included) and runs
deploy/self.yml against localhost. Running it again changes nothing.
```

### dev: the developer's own commands: the project's tracker, CI and checks, not the pool

#### mop dev

```text
the developer's own commands: the project's tracker, CI and checks, not the pool

  mop dev bug   project tracker: GitLab issues, one issue per unit of work
  mop dev ci    pipelines, job logs, lint and runners: GitLab CI from the terminal
  mop dev docs  regenerate docs/CLI.md, the CLI reference, from the docstrings
  mop dev test  run the checks in tests/, all or the named ones
  mop dev controller  isolated PostgreSQL foundation checks in Docker
  mop dev web   build the dashboard (web/dist) and check the committed build

Run from a working copy of the project: the coordinates come from its git
origin, the credentials from .env. The tracker and CI stay on the master's
CLI and are never exposed as MCP tools: the tracker's coordinates resolve
from the package's origin, not the session's working copy, and a tool here
would lead a foreign master into this project's tracker.
```

#### mop dev bug

```text
project tracker: GitLab issues, one issue per unit of work

  mop dev bug list [--all] [--label L] [-t TEXT]   open issues, worst first
  mop dev bug show <iid>                           full body
  mop dev bug new "<title>" [--label L ...]        body from --body, --body-file or stdin
  mop dev bug new "<title>" --epic 12              child of epic #12
  mop dev bug evidence <iid>                       fetched branches and integration merges
  mop dev bug epic <iid>                           the epic's children and progress
  mop dev bug edit <iid> [--title T] [--body TEXT|--body-file F]  replace the title and/or body
  mop dev bug comment <iid> "<text>"               comment (or - for stdin)
  mop dev bug start <iid> [slug] [--no-branch]     claim: status::wip + branch
  mop dev bug close <iid> --comment "..."          close, default status::fixed
  mop dev bug relabel <iid> [--status S]           change labels; live, wip, parked reopen
  mop dev bug labels                               the label vocabulary

Coordinates come from the working copy's git origin; credentials are
GITLAB_TOKEN (or GITLAB_USER + GITLAB_PASSWORD) in .env. Titles, bodies
and comments are in Russian; branch names and commits stay English.
```

#### mop dev bug close

```text
mop dev bug close <iid> [--comment "..."] [--status S]: close an issue, status::fixed by default
```

#### mop dev bug comment

```text
mop dev bug comment <iid> "<text>" | - | --body-file F: comment on an issue
```

#### mop dev bug edit

```text
mop dev bug edit <iid> [--title T] [--body TEXT|--body-file F|-] [--epic N | --no-epic]: change an issue

Replaces the title and/or body from --body, --body-file or stdin (-).
The first-line epic marker survives a body edit unless --epic changes it or
--no-epic removes it. With nothing to change, prints usage.
```

#### mop dev bug epic

```text
mop dev bug epic <iid>: the epic's children and progress
```

#### mop dev bug evidence

```text
mop dev bug evidence <iid>: remote issue branches and verified integration merges

Fetches origin first (updates local remote-tracking refs). Inspects at most
500 listed remote refs, the configured integration branch, 40 integration
refs and 80 first-parent merges per ref. A branch mention or #iid in a commit
message is not evidence of integration; a merge needs a second parent on
that branch. Missing/deleted branch tips cannot be verified.
```

#### mop dev bug labels

```text
mop dev bug labels: the label vocabulary, one from each group per issue

A second label of the same group silently replaces the first.
```

#### mop dev bug list

```text
mop dev bug list [--all] [--label L] [-t TEXT]: open issues, worst first
```

#### mop dev bug new

```text
mop dev bug new "<title>" [--label L ...] [--body TEXT|--body-file F] [--epic N]: open an issue

Body from --body, --body-file or stdin; --epic makes it a child of that epic. A
status label is added when none is given: status::live.
```

#### mop dev bug relabel

```text
mop dev bug relabel <iid> [--status S] [--label L ...]: change labels

--status live, wip or parked also reopens a closed issue; fixed, noise and
dup are closing statuses, but only `mop dev bug close` closes.
```

#### mop dev bug show

```text
mop dev bug show <iid>: the full body of an issue
```

#### mop dev bug start

```text
mop dev bug start <iid> [slug] [--no-branch] [--worker W]: claim an issue

Sets status::wip and, unless --no-branch, creates the issue's branch.
```

#### mop dev chat-probe

```text
mop dev chat-probe [--output DIR] [--timeout seconds] [--history-module /path/session.py]: probe the installed interactive Claude

Uses a fresh home/workdir, a private randomly named tmux server and a loopback
Messages fixture with a dummy key. No existing session is resumed. All responses
are fixture-backed, not paid-provider evidence. Uses --bare to disable discovery
and keychain reads, with explicit Bash/AskUserQuestion tools where supported;
this may expose fewer tools than normal mode. Default permission mode remains
in force. External HTTP/HTTPS proxy attempts are refused; git SSH transports
are disabled and checked before Claude starts. This is not an OS network sandbox.
Managed settings presence refuses launch without reading their contents. Any
unexpected git, marketplace or credential files in its own home fail the run.
Each scenario reports observed, unsupported or unknown independently;
a partial probe is not a claim that every scenario works.

Writes report.json, lossless base64 terminal/input frames, pane snapshots and
fixture request bodies in a new private directory (default: ./chat-probe-UUID).
The directory must not already exist. --timeout is a per-wait bound, 1 to 30
seconds; each scenario is bounded below 120 seconds. Stops only its own tmux
server and fixture listener on exit. Uses a short private /tmp runtime outside
the caller's repository, with explicit tmux -S for every operation. Verifies
owned process PID/start identities after cleanup; leftovers are errors.
Requires installed claude, tmux and git. Temporary runtime is retained privately.

Captures live ready/after-model/after-clear registry, socket peer and key fields
without peerToken values. Optional --history-module explicitly selects a trusted
local regular session.py source (not a downloaded file); invokes its history
before and after /clear and records only safe headers/counts, not private records.

Prints the report path and one verdict per scenario. Exit 1 for runner errors,
not for unsupported or unknown scenarios. Does not contact the pool or load
installation credentials.
```

#### mop dev chat-smoke

```text
mop dev chat-smoke [--output DIR] [--timeout seconds] [--node-root DIR] [--history-root DIR] [--web-root DIR] [--keep-serving]: local fixture-backed chat integration

Runs the fixed trusted tests/_chat_smoke.py helper, excluded from ordinary CI.
Requires installed Claude 2.1.296, tmux and git. Uses a fresh private home,
short own tmux socket and loopback Messages fixture with a dummy API key.
Exercises the actual authenticated HTTP Handler, TerminalBridge, node Registry,
body identity probe and session history source; only transport and identity
storage are local fixtures. No pool, NATS, deployment or paid provider calls.

Optional absolute trusted checkout roots select prerequisite node/history
sources or committed web/dist. Records revision/source hashes and refuses a
source mutation during the run. They are operator-supplied code, not downloads.
The output directory must be new; --timeout bounds each wait to 1..30 seconds.
Prints English JSON progress and a private report path. Unknown and unsupported
scenarios are never passed. Exit 1 means runner error or incomplete required
coverage. Default permission dialogs remain enabled; bare mode can omit tools.
Raw terminal control is a trusted admin capability, not a tmux key filter.

--keep-serving retains only this local fixture for private browser inspection
until interrupted; private report holds its fixture URL and test session token.
Never publish that fixture or use real credentials. Cleanup checks owned process
PID/start identities, attach clients and listener sockets, not foreign sessions.
```

#### mop dev ci

```text
pipelines, job logs, lint and runners: GitLab CI from the terminal

  mop dev ci                           the latest 15 pipelines
  mop dev ci <id> [--failed]           a pipeline's jobs; --failed: only real failures
  mop dev ci show <id> [--failed]      the same
  mop dev ci why <id>                  why it failed: failing jobs with their log tails
  mop dev ci log <job> [--lines N] [--full]
                                       a job's log, the last 60 lines by default
  mop dev ci lint [file]               validate a .gitlab-ci.yml, the working copy's by default
  mop dev ci retry <job>               run a finished job again
  mop dev ci retry --pipeline <id>     rerun a pipeline's failed jobs
  mop dev ci cancel <id>               cancel a pipeline that is still going
  mop dev ci runners                   the project's runners and what each is running

Coordinates and credentials are those of `mop dev bug`: the working copy's git
origin, GITLAB_TOKEN (or GITLAB_USER + GITLAB_PASSWORD) in .env.
```

#### mop dev ci cancel

```text
mop dev ci cancel <id>: cancel a pipeline that is still going

Refused for a pipeline that already finished (success, failed, canceled,
skipped), naming its state: GitLab would accept that and do nothing.
```

#### mop dev ci lint

```text
mop dev ci lint [file]: validate a .gitlab-ci.yml the way GitLab would

The file is the working copy's .gitlab-ci.yml by default; its includes are
resolved. Prints "valid — N job(s): ..." or "invalid" with the errors
(exit 1), then warnings.
```

#### mop dev ci list

```text
mop dev ci list [-n N]: the latest pipelines, newest first

One line each: status, id, short sha, ref, created (UTC), web url.
```

#### mop dev ci log

```text
mop dev ci log <job> [--lines N] [--full]: a job's log

The last 60 lines by default, terminal colors stripped.
```

#### mop dev ci retry

```text
mop dev ci retry <job> | --pipeline <id>: run a job, or a pipeline's failed jobs, again

Refused while the job or pipeline is still going, naming its state. Prints
the new job's id and url; a pipeline retry prints the pipeline's.
```

#### mop dev ci runners

```text
mop dev ci runners: the project's runners and the jobs they are running

A runner per line: ON/OFF (takes work or paused), id, description, status
(whether GitLab sees it), tags. Then each running job and the runner that
holds it.
```

#### mop dev ci show

```text
mop dev ci show <id> [--failed]: a pipeline's jobs

The pipeline's line, then one line per job: status, id, stage, name,
duration. A job marked "(allow_failure)" may fail without failing the
pipeline; --failed lists only the jobs that did fail it.
```

#### mop dev ci why

```text
mop dev ci why <id>: why a pipeline failed

Each job that failed the pipeline, with the last lines of its log. A failed
job with allow_failure is named as one that did NOT fail the pipeline. When
no job failed at all, the pipeline's own reason: a rejected .gitlab-ci.yml
fails with no jobs.
```

#### mop dev controller

```text
mop dev controller [--postgres 16|17] [--check controller|hermetic|usage]: isolated PostgreSQL checks

Runs the selected check with the declared server extra and matching PostgreSQL
client tools in fresh Docker containers, using the same setup as CI. Requires
an existing Docker installation and a mop Git working copy; installs no host
packages and uses no pool. The snapshot contains tracked and nonignored source,
not installation inputs or .git. No host ports, installation credentials or
Docker socket enter test containers. Cleanup failures are reported explicitly.
```

#### mop dev docs

```text
mop dev docs: regenerate docs/CLI.md from the commandlets' docstrings

Writes the CLI reference: every command and verb of `mop` with its whole
docstring, in three parts -- client, server, service. Silent when the file
is written. A commandlet with an empty docstring is refused, named.

The reference is committed: an edit to a commandlet's docstring ships with
the regenerated docs/CLI.md in the same commit, or CI is red.
```

#### mop dev test

```text
mop dev test [name ...] [--strict] [-v]: run the checks in tests/

Every file of tests/ (a helper named _*.py is not a check), or only the
named ones: `mop dev test cli spec`. The checks of the working copy you run
it in; outside one, of the mop that runs it.

  --strict   MOP_TESTS_STRICT=1, as CI: a check that would skip for a missing
             library fails instead
  -v         a line per file as it finishes, not only on a terminal

Prints the output of every file that failed and one line of totals; exit 1
when anything failed.
```

#### mop dev web

```text
the dashboard's build: Vite + React in web/, the result committed in web/dist

  mop dev web build            npm ci and vite build into web/dist
  mop dev web build --check    build aside and compare with web/dist byte for byte
  mop dev web test [file ...]  run the dashboard interaction tests
  mop dev web test --types     check TypeScript
  mop dev web preview         serve the built dashboard locally, without a pool API

Node and npm are the developer's and CI's: the servers get the built dist
with the package and never run node. `--check` is what CI runs on every
push, so a dist that drifted from its sources is red, not silent.
```

#### mop dev web build

```text
mop dev web build [--check]: build the dashboard into web/dist

Runs `npm ci` and `vite build` in web/. Silent when the build lands.

  --check   build into a temporary directory instead and compare it with
            web/dist byte for byte; the differing files are listed and the
            exit code is 1: rebuild with `mop dev web build`

Needs node and npm on this machine (the developer's or CI's), never on a
server.
```

#### mop dev web preview

```text
mop dev web preview [--port N]: serve the built dashboard on localhost

Serves web/dist on 127.0.0.1:4173 by default, without a pool API.
Build first with `mop dev web build`. Stop with Ctrl+C.
```

#### mop dev web test

```text
mop dev web test [file ...] [--types]: check the dashboard

Runs Vitest in web/, optionally restricted to the named test files.
With --types, runs TypeScript checking instead of interaction tests.
Install dependencies first with `mop dev web build`.
```

### driver: node driver: in what a puppet lives

#### mop driver

```text
node driver: in what a puppet lives

  mop driver                     drivers in the registry, and this node's one
  mop driver list                bodies standing on this node — no Nomad needed
  mop driver run <name>          raise the body and run the puppet inside it
  mop driver sweep [--dry]       destroy bodies with no puppet left in them
  mop driver clone-work <dir>    may a session-less clone go (the watchdog asks)
  mop driver build [project|origin] [--fresh] [--force]
                                 bake the project's image on the hypervisors;
                                 no argument: this working copy, .mop as it lies

`run` raises the body and holds its session: everything about the body
happens on the node that owns it, in whatever that node's driver is.
```

#### mop driver build

```text
mop driver build [project|origin] [--fresh] [--force] [--node NAME] [--branch NAME]: bake the project's image

On the hypervisors, from the control machine. No argument: this working
copy, .mop as it lies. Incremental by default: a copy of the image
takes what changed; --fresh builds from the base image anew. The project's
puppets on container nodes are stopped, their bodies destroyed and raised
again from the new image; a busy puppet refuses unless --force.
--node NAME: on that node only — its puppets alone are stopped, the others'
image and work are left as they are.
--branch NAME: read .mop from that remote branch, not the local tree;
pin the source mirror to the same commit for cache warm-up. It replaces
the project's image on the selected nodes, not a separate branch image.
Without --branch the local-tree/default-branch behavior is unchanged.
```

#### mop driver clone-work

```text
mop driver clone-work <dir>: may a clone with no live session be removed — exit 0 yes, 3 no

Asked by the disk watchdog's host tier for each clone whose puppet has no
tmux session. The answer is the pool's one rule of work in a clone:
uncommitted, unpushed, or off its home branch holds work, and a clone that
cannot be read is kept. A directory without .git is no clone and may go.
Prints the reason on one line. Any exit other than 0 and 3 is a failed
check, not a verdict: the watchdog keeps the clone and says so.
```

#### mop driver exec

```text
run a command in an existing body: mop driver exec <name> -- <command> [args...]

Operator-only, run on the node. Uses the node's driver and an existing body,
not a Claude prompt or a second session. Arguments remain literal through
the driver's remote shell; a nonzero child exit remains nonzero. Does not copy or display any
credentials and does not create, restart or stop the body.
```

#### mop driver list

```text
mop driver list: bodies standing on this node — no Nomad needed

The roster of this machine, asked from its driver: on a hypervisor the
containers, on a host node the live tmux servers. Runs on the node itself.
```

#### mop driver purge-clone

```text
remove a deleted host puppet's data: mop driver purge-clone <name> --orphan

Run on the host node after verifying that the job was deleted on the
controller. Removes only that puppet's clone and target cache. Refuses
container drivers, live or unknown tmux sessions, unsafe paths and symlinks.
--orphan explicitly confirms that the job is no longer registered; this is
not an automatic sweep and may remove unsaved work.
```

#### mop driver run

```text
mop driver run <name>: raise the body and run the puppet inside it

What the job spec calls (the outer wrapper). Runs on the node that owns the
puppet: ensure the body, bootstrap the sandbox through the server,
push the inner wrapper in and hold its session until it ends.
```

#### mop driver sweep

```text
mop driver sweep [--dry]: destroy bodies with no puppet left in them

The disk watchdog's tier for a node whose bodies are objects of their own.
Runs on the node, knows nothing of Nomad. A body is destroyed only when its
tmux answers with no session and its clone holds no work (or there is no
clone at all); a body whose clone holds work, whose clone cannot be read, or
which does not answer is kept and named. Refuses when no body at all has a
session.
```

### node: pool nodes: mop node [drain|up|forget <name>]

#### mop node

```text
pool nodes: mop node [drain|up|forget <name>]

  mop node                 what the pool stands on: driver, projects, capacity
  mop node drain <name>    move its puppets off and close it to the scheduler
  mop node up <name>       open it to the scheduler again
  mop node forget <name>   drop it from the roster

Draining is graceful: a puppet leaves with its clone intact. `forget`
refuses while anything still runs there, and while the node is in the
inventory — the next deploy would configure it from again.
```

#### mop node drain

```text
mop node drain <name>: move its puppets off and close it to the scheduler

Graceful: the wrapper takes its session down on TERM, so a puppet leaves
with its clone intact.
```

#### mop node forget

```text
mop node forget <name>: drop the node from the roster

Refuses while anything still runs there — a node dropped from under a live
puppet keeps working and the master never hears of it again.

Refuses as well while the node is in the controller's inventory: the next
mop server deploy would configure it again. Take it out of the inventory and run
mop server deploy first.
```

#### mop node up

```text
mop node up <name>: open the node to the scheduler again
```

### project: pool projects: mop project [add <git-origin>|delete <name>|list]

#### mop project

```text
pool projects: mop project [add <git-origin>|delete <name>|list]

  mop project              what the pool serves: one line per project
  mop project add [origin] register a project for the pool
                           (default: this working copy's origin)
  mop project delete <name> take it off the pool
  mop project limit [<name> <N|none>]  puppet limit of a project
  mop project list [--origins]  the same list, for scripts

A project is one repository and one slice of the pool; its name is the
basename of its origin, and puppet names are built from it.
```

#### mop project add

```text
make a project ready: mop project add [--update|--rebuild] [--node NAME] [--branch NAME] [-v] [git-origin]

Without origin, the origin of the current working copy is used.

Registers the project on the server (operator's verb project_add)
and builds its image from .mop/sandbox.yaml on the container nodes through the server's builder when it is missing on
any of them. Afterwards `mop add` can place a puppet right away.

  --update    build the image even if it exists, incrementally
  --rebuild   build it from the base image
  --node NAME build on this node only: its puppets alone are stopped and
              raised again, the other nodes keep their image and their work
  --branch NAME read .mop and warm-up sources from that remote branch,
                pinned to one commit; update even an existing image
  -v          print every line of the build's output, not only on a terminal

One image per project and node: --branch replaces it, not a new image
name. It does not set the puppet's working or landing branch.
Without --branch, the default remote branch is used.

Idempotent without --branch: run it again after changing the project's .mop. Silent when all
goes well; on a terminal it shows the current step under the last lines of
the build's output, and erases both when done.
```

#### mop project delete

```text
take a project off the pool: mop project delete <name>

The project leaves the pool together with its puppet limit; its puppets
lose the bus. Refuses while the project still has puppets — they would keep
working with no one able to reach them — delete its puppets first
(mop delete pu-<project>-<n>). The repository is not touched.
```

#### mop project limit

```text
puppet limit of a project: mop project limit [<name> <N|none>]

  mop project limit                 every project's limit
  mop project limit rugent 3        at most 3 puppets for rugent
  mop project limit rugent 0        frozen: no new puppets
  mop project limit rugent none     no limit

The limit is the project's, not a person's: the cluster service sees which
project a request is about, not who sent it. It is checked by the add verb
(mop add), against the project's jobs that are not dead; puppets already
running above a newly lowered limit are left alone.

Kept on the server and set by the operator's verb project_limit; the
service reads it on every add, so no restart is needed.
```

#### mop project list

```text
projects the pool serves: mop project list [--origins]

--origins prints the origins themselves; without it, project names.
```

### secret: project secrets: mop secret file|var add|list|remove

#### mop secret

```text
project secrets: mop secret file|var add|list|remove

  mop secret file add <path>...     files of this working copy, kept on the server
  mop secret file list              what the project has: name and size
  mop secret file remove <name>...
  mop secret var add VAR=VALUE...   variables for the puppets' sessions
  mop secret var list               names only: a list is no way to read a secret
  mop secret var remove VAR...

The project is this working copy's, the server its binding (mop login). The
server keeps them and every puppet of the project gets them at each
start: files in the root of its clone, variables in its session. A puppet
already running gets a change at its next start (mop recycle).
```

#### mop secret file

```text
secret files of the project: mop secret file add|list|remove

mop secret file add <path>...     a file of this working copy; on the puppets
                                  it lands at the same path in the clone
mop secret file list
mop secret file remove <name>...
```

#### mop secret var

```text
secret variables of the project: mop secret var add|list|remove

mop secret var add VAR=VALUE...   in the environment of every puppet's session
mop secret var list               names only
mop secret var remove VAR...
```

### session: private live-session history and terminal control: mop session <verb>

#### mop session

```text
private live-session history and terminal control: mop session <verb>

  mop session history <name> [--cursor cursor]
  mop session terminal <name> <action> [tid] [options]

History follows the current conversation. Terminal attaches to the same tmux
session, never a second Claude process. Terminal control is an operator-only
capability: it can execute commands in the body. No automatic input replay.
```

#### mop session history

```text
mop session history <name> [--cursor cursor]: read private conversation records

Returns bounded JSON with epoch, session_id, cursor, records, reset, has_more
and partial. Keep the returned cursor for the next read; a reset replaces the
old live conversation. Incomplete JSON lines remain pending. This is not a
token stream. No arbitrary transcript path is accepted.
```

#### mop session terminal

```text
mop session terminal <name> <action> [tid] [options]: private terminal RPC

Actions: open, read, input, interrupt, resize, close.
  open       --mode ro|rw --cols N --rows N (default ro, 100 by 30)
  read       --cursor N --wait N (default 0, at most 15 seconds)
  input      --seq N --data BASE64 (at most 4096 decoded bytes)
  interrupt  --seq N (Escape to the existing CLI, not job stop)
  resize     --cols N --rows N (writer only)
  close      detaches this client, never kills the puppet

Open returns a private tid. Every subsequent action needs it. Input sequences
start at 1 and advance consecutively; an unknown receipt must not be retried
with a new sequence. Terminal output is base64 bytes for an emulator, not text
with terminal escapes removed. Operator-only node verbs enforce read-only and ownership.
```

## Server

Run on the installation's server, the controller, not on a client.

### server: the installation's server: commands run on the controller, not on a client

#### mop server

```text
the installation's server: commands run on the controller, not on a client

  mop server deploy      roll out the pool: Nomad, the bus, the agent, the disk watchdog
  mop server config      the installation's settings and where each one comes from
  mop server setup       this controller's own dependencies: ansible, rsync, git, libraries
  mop server user        people of the operators file: add, passwd, delete, import
  mop server cluster     the cluster service: Nomad behind the bus
  mop server bootstrap   what the server plays at every start of a sandbox
  mop server web         the pool's dashboard in a browser (unit mop-web)
  mop server callout     the bus's auth callout (unit mop-callout)
  mop server pve-facts   a Proxmox node's image and build facts, for the build playbook

These need what lives only on the controller: the inventory, the
playbooks, secrets/ and the Nomad token.
```

#### mop server bootstrap

```text
sandbox bootstrap: what the server plays at every start of a sandbox

  mop server bootstrap serve            the server's subscriber (unit mop-bootstrap)
  mop server bootstrap check            is the service answering on the bus, and for
                                 which puppets it holds a workspace

A puppet's workspace (.mop/bootstrap.yaml) is played by the server into its
sandbox at every start, before the session opens (docs/BOOTSTRAP.md). It is
the puppet's, not the project's: mop add, mop update and mop recycle
send it from the working copy they run in, an absent file removes it, and
mop delete takes it away. The project's sandbox.yaml goes into its image
(mop project add).
```

#### mop server bootstrap check

```text
mop server bootstrap check: is the service answering on the bus, and for which puppets it holds a workspace
```

#### mop server bootstrap serve

```text
mop server bootstrap serve: the server's subscriber (unit mop-bootstrap)

Plays a project's .mop/bootstrap.yaml into a sandbox when its node asks
at start (docs/BOOTSTRAP.md).
```

#### mop server callout

```text
mop server callout: the bus's auth callout (unit mop-callout)

On the server, as the pool user. Handles authentication for people —
checked by the identity provider, keeping their rights, only over
WebSocket — and for puppets, checked against the server's own password
files. docs/BUS.md.
```

#### mop server cluster

```text
cluster service: mop server cluster [serve|check|users|reload|builder|export] — Nomad behind the bus

  mop server cluster check    is the service answering, and does it see Nomad
  mop server cluster serve    the server's subscriber (unit mop-cluster)
  mop server cluster users    write the bus users file from the server's registry
  mop server cluster reload   make nats reread its config, and check it took
  mop server cluster builder  the server's image builder (unit mop-builder)
  mop server cluster export   write the registry as a legacy pair for a rollback

The only one on the installation that talks to Nomad on someone else's
behalf: masters and operators ask, the service checks that they may —
the management token never leaves the server.
```

#### mop server cluster builder

```text
mop server cluster builder: the server's image builder (unit mop-builder)

Listens on mop.admin.build.rpc and builds a project's image on the
hypervisors when an operator asks, streaming the build's steps back. Runs as
the controller's user: the playbook needs its inventory and ssh keys.
```

#### mop server cluster check

```text
mop server cluster check: is the service answering on the bus, and does it see Nomad
```

#### mop server cluster export

```text
mop server cluster export <DIR> [--json]: write the registry as a legacy pair for a rollback

On the server, as the pool user. Reads the live snapshot
(~/.config/mop/projects.json) once, validates it, and lays the pair
(projects, limits.json) out in a NEW directory DIR with a completion
marker export.json; nothing in the live registry, the legacy pair or
the bus is touched, and the command stops no writers.

An ordinary success prints nothing (the summary is a machine matter:
the library return and the export.json marker, not terminal prose);
--json prints the summary as one JSON object for scripts. Refusals
print their reason to stderr and exit non-zero, without echoing the
contents of a corrupt file or any origin credentials.

The rollback itself is an operator's procedure: stop every writer, take
a final export, verify the sha256 in export.json against the source,
then switch. The command does not perform the switch and does not
repair bare names, collisions or orphan limits -- the validator refuses
them, and how to resolve each is a separate decision.
The export carries origin credentials as its private data: the
directory is 0700, the files are 0600, and summaries, markers and
refusals name paths, counts and digests -- never a URL or a token.
An existing destination (file, directory, symlink, or a concurrent
claim) is a refusal: the command never overwrites, and a failed attempt
removes only what that attempt itself created.
```

#### mop server cluster reload

```text
mop server cluster reload: make nats-server reread its config, and check it took

On the server, as the pool user. Checks the file with `nats-server -t`,
sends SIGHUP, then compares the running config's digest (/varz on the
loopback monitoring port) with the file's. A rejected reload -- nats keeps
the old config and says so only in its journal -- is a refusal with the
reason, not a silent success.
```

#### mop server cluster serve

```text
mop server cluster serve: the server's subscriber (unit mop-cluster)

Listens on mop.*.cluster.rpc and answers the pool's verbs over Nomad —
the roster, a puppet's life cycle, the nodes. The job spec is built here,
never accepted from the asker.
```

#### mop server cluster users

```text
mop server cluster users [--reload]: write the bus users file from the server's registry

On the server, as the pool user. Reads the people, services and nodes that
mop server deploy put into /etc/nats/base-users.json, the projects from the
server's registry (~/.config/mop/projects.json), gives a project without a bus
password a new one, and writes /etc/nats/users.conf (the machines) and
/etc/nats/callout.conf with the auth callout's keys.
--reload sends nats-server SIGHUP when users.conf changed and checks that
nats took it; a changed callout.conf needs a restart instead, and --reload
refuses rather than fire a reload nats would reject.
```

#### mop server config

```text
settings of this installation: mop server config [--json | set KEY VALUE]

Shows what the system runs on right now and where each value came from: an
environment variable outranks .env, .env outranks the default in the code.

Defaults intentionally equal the cluster's current values: .env is in
.gitignore, and a fresh clone without it must still come up as-is. The only
things required in .env are secrets.

set KEY VALUE changes one declared setting in the controller's .env,
atomically and without displaying its value. It does not reconfigure running
services: apply the installation through the normal deployment gate.
MOP_SOUL_ROLES accepts 1 to enable or an empty value to disable.
```

#### mop server controller

```text
mop server controller <action>: isolated Django controller maintenance

Fresh-install foundation only; never imports old state or contacts HTTP/NATS.

  setup --venv PATH             install the declared server extra in a new venv
  check                         Django system checks and schema readiness
  migrate                       apply standard Django migrations
  migrations-check              refuse uncommitted model changes
  initialize                    bind the empty schema to protected trust roots
  admin --username NAME         create initial admin; password is read privately
  serve --host host --port N    production ASGI server (one process)
    --hostname name             allowed public hostname (repeatable)
    --tls-cert PATH --tls-key PATH  native HTTPS; required for non-loopback bind
  worker                        run the bounded worker lifecycle
  backup --file PATH            protected PostgreSQL custom-format dump
  restore --file PATH           restore into an empty DB, reset epoch, disable effects

Every action except setup requires an explicit absolute MOP_CONTROLLER_BOOTSTRAP
file. Maintenance uses its own DB principal with schema/backup rights. Web and
workers use distinct runtime principals without DDL/role/database creation rights;
only maintenance can read the encryption root. Django signing material is a
separate protected file. Supply secrets in these files, never in CLI arguments.
Restore requires stopped services and an empty target; no legacy import exists.
```

#### mop server deploy

```text
deploy: mop server deploy [--check] [--skip-pipeline] [--from-ci]

The whole installation in one run; no separate targets — rerunning is
cheaper than remembering which target owned what. Machines only:
projects come and go with `mop project add|delete`, deploy takes no
arguments.

--check: ansible's check mode with --diff — nothing changes, and
nothing runs after the playbook. With MOP_DEPLOY_NEEDS_GREEN=1 deploy
refuses unless HEAD's pipeline on the default branch is green;
--skip-pipeline is the emergency way past and says so. --from-ci is
what CI runs on the server: default branch, fetch, fast-forward, the
gate mandatory; when the gate's only answer would be "wait" because
HEAD has moved past the commit that started the job, it exits 0 — the
newer job deploys it.
```

#### mop server diagnose

```text
mop server diagnose: offline summary of this installation only

Reports two local facts, no network, no migration, no writes: where each
effective setting of this installation comes from (the same resolver as
`mop server config`, values themselves are not printed here), and what
the local project registry runs on -- a v1 snapshot, the legacy pair of
files, or nothing yet. This is not the registry of a remote selected
server; client-side selection is `mop diagnose`.

A registry that cannot be read refuses with exit code 1 naming the file;
a missing registry is informational: exit code 0 with an explicit
not-ready line.
```

#### mop server disk

```text
space on pool nodes: mop server disk [node]

df on the filesystem where puppet clones and target directories live.
This is a node-level verb run only on the server: host space belongs
to the whole pool, not to one project.
```

#### mop server doctor

```text
pool diagnostics: mop server doctor [group] [--fix [--safe]]

Catches stuck puppets, a stale login, restart backoff, exhausted quota,
and a job spec older than the node driver. Without an argument every
group runs; an unknown group name is refused with the list.

--fix treats what is treatable; a silent node agent is left alone — the
puppet may be working, and a restart would kill that work. --fix --safe
treats only what cannot break work (login+nudge, disk sweep) and names
the rest: restarts, stops, /model and spec updates stay the operator's
call. The server runs --fix --safe hourly (mop-doctor.timer).
```

#### mop server gc

```text
recycle free puppets on nodes low on space: mop server gc [--dry]

A node with less than MOP_GC_FREE_MIN_GB free gets its free puppets
recycled (clone reset to HEAD, target wiped) — no more than
MOP_GC_MAX_PER_RUN per run. Run this on the server, not from a master shell: disk pressure on a node
is a fact about every tenant, not one project.
```

#### mop server grant

```text
revoke one role principal: mop server grant revoke <principal> [--cut]

Controller-only. Selects the exact grant identifier, never a reusable puppet
name or a project-wide match. Revocation is idempotent and denies further role
operations without stopping the body or its current work.

--cut also removes this principal's stored password. Existing bus connections
retain their transport permissions until reconnecting; this is not a forced
disconnect and cannot erase credentials or secrets already delivered to a body.
```

#### mop server proxykey

```text
client proxy key rotation: mop server proxykey start|resume|status — on the controller

  mop server proxykey start --nodes n1,n2 --exclusive   frozen recipient set, explicit nodes
  mop server proxykey start --all-registered --exclusive  full known node set, offline included
  mop server proxykey start --no-recipients --exclusive   deliberate empty recipient set
  mop server proxykey resume --exclusive
  mop server proxykey status [--json]

One writer, one operation, checkpoints all the way (the rotation
library). The verbs are a thin front: the adapter supplies the real effects —
loopback management API of the installed proxy, client-key probes — and
every decision stays in the library. Works on the controller only; a
puppet context is refused before any network or file touch.

start requires --exclusive: the caller affirms no other writer (panel,
deploy) is active — the upstream has no compare-and-swap. The recipient
set is frozen at start: offline nodes stay recipients, resume never
re-selects membership. Quiet on a fast success; pending or refusal is
rc 1 with a safe reason (no key material anywhere in the output).
```

#### mop server proxykey resume

```text
resume the rotation: mop server proxykey resume --exclusive

Drives the recorded operation from its checkpoints to the first
blocker: the rotation library decides every step; the adapter
supplies the effects. The frozen recipient set stands as recorded;
membership is never re-selected. Pending or refusal is rc 1 with a
safe reason; a quiet fast success prints one line. --exclusive
affirms the caller is still the only writer.
```

#### mop server proxykey start

```text
start a rotation: mop server proxykey start --nodes n1,n2 --exclusive

Checks the controller boundary, resolves the controller source and the
cluster service copy, freezes the recipient set (--nodes, or
--all-registered for the full known node set, offline included, or
--no-recipients), and records the private checkpoint. No proxy effect:
the remote steps belong to resume. A recorded operation is a quiet rc 0
(one JSON line with --json); a refusal is rc 1 with its reason.
--exclusive affirms the caller is the
only writer (panel included); without it the command refuses.
```

#### mop server proxykey status

```text
the rotation status: mop server proxykey status [--json]

Reads the private checkpoint and prints the library's safe projection:
stage, per-recipient codes, refusal reasons — never a key, never a raw
agent tail. No operation is a quiet zero; an invalid state file is rc 1
with the validator's reason.
```

#### mop server pve-facts

```text
mop server pve-facts --base N [--project P --listing TEXT]: the pve driver's facts as JSON

One hypervisor's facts from its VMID base (the host's inventory line):
the bodies' network, gateway and prefix, the routes, the wrapper path,
the body key and known_hosts, the top of its VMID range. With --project
also its image and build body, and the project's bodies standing there;
--listing is the wrapper's `list` output on that node.

Controller-side facts for the image build and the hypervisor role.
```

#### mop server setup

```text
this controller's own dependencies: mop server setup

Sets up the machine that runs mop server deploy, and nothing for the pool:
the pool's nodes and bodies are ansible's business (mop server deploy).
Installs ansible with the ansible.posix collection, rsync, git, curl, pip
and the python libraries mop is written on. An operator's machine has its
own: mop setup.

Ansible does the work, as everywhere else in mop: this command only
installs ansible itself through apt when it is missing (Debian 13 ships
the full ansible package, collections included) and runs
deploy/self.yml against localhost. Running it again changes nothing.
```

#### mop server sweep

```text
garbage on the pool's nodes: mop server sweep [--dry]

Destroys orphan bodies — those no job names any more — and only lists
build bodies: a running sealed image is either a live build or a broken
one, and they look the same from here. --dry lists without destroying.
Run on the server, not a master shell: what stands on a node is every
tenant's fact. `mop driver sweep` is the node half: it judges by the
absence of a tmux session.
```

#### mop server user

```text
people of the operators file: mop server user add|passwd|delete|import — on the server

  mop server user add <login> --role admin|user [--projects a,b|*] [--name "..."] [--email ...] [--stdin]
  mop server user passwd <login> [--stdin]
  mop server user delete <login>
  mop server user import      transitional: move MOP_OPERATORS into the file, passwords kept

People live in the identity provider: with MOP_AUTH_PROVIDER=file, in
the operators file on the server (~/.config/mop/secrets/operators, or
MOP_OPERATORS_FILE), one line per person, the password as a scrypt hash.
With file,ldap (a chain) the file holds local people on top of LDAP and
mop server user edits it; with ldap alone they live in LDAP, and mop server user refuses.

Works on the server, where the file lives. The password is asked twice
without echo, or read as one line from stdin with --stdin. The server's
services (callout, the identity verb) read a copy in /etc/nats/identity: mop
user refreshes it when it can, otherwise it says to run mop server deploy.
```

#### mop server user add

```text
add a person: mop server user add <login> --role admin|user [--projects a,b|*] [--name "..."] [--email ...] [--stdin]

Refuses a login already in the operators file or in MOP_OPERATORS. The role
and projects follow MOP_OPERATORS: admin is the whole pool and takes no
projects; user takes a list, or * for every project. The password is asked
twice without echo, or read as one line from stdin with --stdin. Name and
email sign the person's puppet commits. Silent when all goes well.
```

#### mop server user delete

```text
remove a person: mop server user delete <login>

Takes the person's line out of the operators file; the next connection is
refused. Connections already open live on. Silent when all goes well.
```

#### mop server user import

```text
transitional: move MOP_OPERATORS into the operators file: mop server user import

Every MOP_OPERATORS entry becomes a line of the file with its current
password (the one mop server deploy made in secrets/nats-op-<login>.pass, now as a
hash), its role and projects; name and email are empty (mop server user delete and
add again, or edit the line). All or nothing: a login already in the file,
or one without a password, refuses the whole move. The operator.json on
people's machines keeps working, no new mop join.

Afterwards remove MOP_OPERATORS from .env and run mop server deploy: until then
each moved login is defined twice and refused. Goes away together with
MOP_OPERATORS.
```

#### mop server user passwd

```text
set a person's password: mop server user passwd <login> [--stdin]

The password is asked twice without echo, or read as one line from stdin
with --stdin; the rest of the person's line stays. A login still in
MOP_OPERATORS is refused: mop server user import moves it into the file first.
Silent when all goes well.
```

#### mop server web

```text
pool dashboard on the web: mop server web [--port N] [--bind ADDR]

`mop list`, `mop node` and `mop stat` on one page, refreshed in place:

  /            the page, /assets/N its files, /logo.png
  /api/pool    snapshot as JSON; /events — the same as SSE,
               plus an `operation` frame when a click reaches its verdict
  /healthz     200 once the first snapshot is in
  /api/session the session; /api/login and /api/logout by JSON post
               (file/LDAP, bus identity)
  /api/journal the full journal, admin only; the public feeds none

The overview is available without login; logging in opens the admin side —
the journal and the proxy panel. Admin clicks ride the shared workflow
as a thread-per-operation executor: the verdict lands as an SSE `operation`
frame and an ops.record audit line in the journal. Port and bind:
MOP_WEB_PORT (9000), MOP_WEB_BIND (127.0.0.1); beyond — the TLS proxy.
```

## Service

Started by systemd and the job spec, not by hand.

### service: managed services (not for interactive use)

#### mop agent

```text
node agent: answers the bus about the puppets on this node (unit mop-agent)

  mop agent            subscribe and serve, until stopped
  mop agent --check    ask this node's agent over the bus whether it answers

One per node, under systemd, outside the job spec (docs/BUS.md): it must
answer precisely while a puppet is restarting.
```

#### mop mcp

```text
mop mcp [--check]: expose pool commands as tools

Started by a claude session. --check shows the local profile and connection
settings; the available tools depend on the session's access.
```
